_about: Party makeup of each legislative chamber for the session starting in 2027, after the November 3, 2026 elections (holdover senators included; D includes Minnesota's DFL and North Dakota's Democratic-NPL; I independents, P Vermont Progressives, G Greens; 'uncalled' seats not yet decided; 'vacant' empty seats), the governor serving in 2027 [name, party, how], any bipartisan coalition running a chamber, and a confidence flag: 'called' (control clear), 'close' (control or a supermajority depends on uncalled races), 'unknown'. Unofficial results as reported by news outlets, AP calls and Wikipedia's election pages; nothing was certified yet. States with no 2026 legislative election (LA, MS, NJ, VA; and KS, NM and SC Senates) show their current makeup. Nebraska's one house is nonpartisan. For a one-off 'after the election' view; not kept up to date. Checked against opened sources the same day (elected_2026_check.json): control, supermajorities and governors confirmed; TX House, UT House, NV Assembly and the AK governor corrected.

S.note: Holdovers (10 seats not up): 5 D, 5 R (pre-election 9 D, 11 R; seats up were 6 R, 4 D). Called: A Stedman R, E Giessel R, Q R; G, I, K D. C is R either way (all three candidates Republican; Stutes leads). Uncalled until ranked-choice tabulation Nov 18 (certification Nov 25): M (Tilton R 32.9, Berry R 32.6, Chesbro D 28.7), O (Rauscher R 42.9, Sheldon R 30.6, Bauer D 26.1), S (Edgmon I 37.6, Deacon R 26.3, Guy D 24.3; formerly Hoffman D). By leaders: D 8, R 11, I 1.

H.note: Called seats per MultiState's race table (I = nonpartisan/undeclared). Uncalled (ADN Nov 10 leaders): 6 Vance R, 11 Coulombe R, 23 Allard R, 24 McCarty R vs Wall R, 25 D. Johnson R, 27 (not reported), 28 Wright R vs Moore R, 29 Nelson R, 30 McCabe R vs Massie R, 33 Prax R, 34 Cottle I, 37 Trefon D, 38 Jimmie D vs McCormick D, 39 (not reported). Rough lean: about 16 D, 16-17 R, 6 I. Ranked-choice tabulation Nov 18.

governor: newly elected (won 50.8% of first choices; ADN, Nov 13)
ak.note: Coalitions keep control of both chambers; House coalition grows; Democrats flipped at least two Republican House seats. Party counts not final until Nov 18 ranked-choice tabulation. Bipartisan coalitions announced Nov 5 for the 35th Legislature. Senate: Cathy Giessel (R) to be President; coalition at 11 (bare majority) per Alaska Public Media, after three Republicans (Bjorkman, Stedman, Merrick) were in talks to leave the 14-member group for the all-Republican minority; could grow to 16-17 with a deal. House: Calvin Schrage (I) to be Speaker; majority of Democrats and independents at 22-23 depending on pending races, possibly 24-25 with moderate Republicans (outgoing coalition was 21).

S.note: All 35 up. Was 27 R, 8 D. Democrats gained SD-2 and SD-7. SD-10 uncalled: Jesse Battles (I) leads Sen. Andrew Jones (R) by fewer than 100 votes, likely automatic recount (Wikipedia's table counts it as I: 24-10-1).

H.note: All 105 up. Was 76 R, 29 D; Democrats gained HD-15 and HD-25.

al.note: Republicans keep two-thirds in both chambers (Senate 24 of 35 exactly, 25 if Jones wins SD-10). Alabama overrides vetoes by simple majority.

S.note: 18 seats on the ballot (MultiState lists 18 races; Wikipedia says 17 of 35 up), the rest holdovers. Was 29-6; Democrats flipped SD-13 (Allison Sweatman beat Brandon Achor).

H.note: All 100 up. Was 80-20 (counting a vacant seat last held by Republicans); 10 R-to-D flips.

ar.note: House Republicans lose three-fourths (75 needed for most appropriations); still over two-thirds. Senate Republicans keep three-fourths. Veto override is a simple majority.

S.note: Was 17 R, 13 D. AP had called 17 D by Nov 6 with Democrats leading the other three; MultiState gives the split as 20-10 for Democrats.

H.note: Was 33 R, 27 D. Called seats 37-22; the last seat (second LD-27 seat) is between two Republicans (Lisa Fink leads Tony Rivero by under 400 votes, inside the automatic-recount margin), so it is R either way.

az.note: Democrats flip both chambers (first Democratic control and trifecta since 1966). Senate D 20 of 30 is two-thirds (veto overrides need two-thirds).

S.note: 20 even-numbered seats up: 16 D, 2 R (SD-4, SD-12) called; Democrats flipped SD-36 and SD-40. Uncalled (both Republican-held): SD-6 (Niello R 51%, Frame D 49% per CSBA Nov 11) and SD-32 (Seyarto R vs Tate D). Holdovers derived as 16 D, 4 R from a pre-election 30-10 (Wikipedia). CSBA (Nov 11) said Democrats held 29 before the election, which would make this D 31, R 7: treat holdover counts as approximate.

A.note: All 80 up. Was 60 D, 19 R, 1 vacant. AD-72 uncalled (Van Der Mark R 50.3%, Kluwe D 49.7%). Wikipedia infobox and MultiState both give 67-12. CSBA (Nov 11) also listed AD-33 (R lead), AD-70 and AD-74 (D leads) as too close to call.

ca.note: Democrats keep and grow two-thirds supermajorities (54 Assembly, 27 Senate); largest Democratic Assembly caucus in modern history.

S.note: 18 seats up (MultiState lists 21 races, incl. vacancy elections), rest holdovers. Was 23-12; Democrats flipped SD-30, the only Senate flip.

H.note: All 65 up. Was 43-22; Democrats flipped HD-15, 16, 19, 21, 50, 51 (HD-21 and HD-51 about 51-49 in late counts).

co.note: Democrats gain two-thirds in both chambers (Senate exactly 24 of 35; House 49, 44 needed).

S.note: All 36 up. Was 25-11. Senate GOP leader Stephen Harding lost. SD-34 (Wallingford): Democrat Brandi Mandato led Sen. Paul Cicarella (R) by about 24 votes, recount; counted D here as in Wikipedia's infobox (32-4 if Cicarella wins).

H.note: All 151 up. Was 102-49. Two mandatory recounts: HD-62 (Kim Becker D led Rep. Mark Anderson R by 34) and HD-71 (William Pizzuto R led by 4); counted as led.

ct.note: Democrats expand two-thirds supermajorities (24 Senate, 101 House needed for overrides); 33-3 is unofficial but stated by CT Public and Wikipedia.

S.note: 11 of 21 up; no seat changed party.

H.note: All 41 up. Was 27-14; Democrats flipped HD-4, HD-9, HD-34.

de.note: Democrats gain two-thirds of the House (28 needed) to go with the Senate's (14), enough for constitutional amendments without Republicans; already above three-fifths for veto overrides.

S.note: 20 of 40 up. I = Jason Pizzo (no party). Vacant: SD-39 (Bryan Avila, R, resigned Aug 2026 to run for lieutenant governor; heavily Republican, special election not yet held as of Sept). Wikipedia and MultiState give R 26 (counting that seat); another report gives 25 R, 13 D, 1 NPA plus the vacancy.

H.note: All 120 up. Was 86-34. HD-33: Daniel McDow (D) beat Rep. Monique Miller (R) by under 300 votes, headed to recount; counted D.

fl.note: Republicans lose two-thirds in both chambers (80 House, 27 Senate needed for veto overrides); House Republicans also below three-fifths (72) needed to put constitutional amendments on the ballot.

S.note: All 56 up. Was 33-23; Democrats flipped SD-37, 42, 45, 48.

H.note: All 180 up. Was 99 R, 81 D. Democrats have 91 called seats, exactly the majority. Uncalled: HD-103 (Chris Luchey D leads Rep. Soo Hong R by about 27-35 votes, recount possible), HD-154 (Gerald Greene R leads Harry James D by about 261 after 388 uncounted Seminole County votes were found on a memory card; probe under way), HD-151 (Dec 1 runoff, Mike Cheokas R vs Wolfe D). By leaders and the runoff seat counted R, 92-88 (Wikipedia); Georgia Recorder (Nov 9) reported 91-89.

ga.note: Democrats flip the House (first time since 2004), on a one- or two-seat margin; Republicans keep the Senate 29-27.

S.note: 13 of 25 up; election left it 22-3, then Sen. Brenton Awa (former minority leader) left the Republican Party Nov 6 to become an independent; Samantha DeCorte is the new minority leader.

H.note: All 51 up. Was 41-10. Democrats gained HD-18, 32, 39; Green Pa'ele Kiakona appears to have won HD-14 (uncured Maui ballots remain).

hi.note: Democrats keep two-thirds in both chambers; first Green Party legislator in the House.

S.note: 25 of 50 up (odd districts), 25 holdovers. Was 33-17; Democrats flipped SD-21 and SD-47, Republicans SD-35. Wikipedia's text elsewhere says 31-18 (likely a vacancy or typo); MultiState and Wikipedia's table give 32-18.

H.note: All 100 up. Was 67-33. HD-19 uncalled: Rep. Brent Siegrist (R) leads by a few dozen votes (56-44 if he holds).

ia.note: Republicans lose the two-thirds House supermajority (67) they won in 2024; the Senate was already below 34 before the election and stays there.

S.note: All 35 up. Was 29-6.

H.note: All 70 up. Was 61-9.

id.note: Republicans keep two-thirds in both chambers (24 Senate, 47 House).

S.note: Wikipedia's 2026 Illinois Senate election page: 45-14 (was 40-19); the page is flagged as not yet updated district by district. Capitol News Illinois (Nov 4): D 44 with 3 races uncalled, could reach 46-13; by Nov 6 Republican Dave Syverson (SD 35) had pulled slightly ahead. Totals include the 20 holdover senators. Unofficial.

H.note: No final count found. Capitol News Illinois, Nov 4: D 80 (up from 78) with 7 House races uncalled, could reach 85-33. By Nov 6 Republican Jeff Keicher (HD 70) had pulled ahead. Speaker Welch's caucus claimed at least 4 pickups. R 31 = 118 - 80 - 7.

il.note: Democrats keep and expand their three-fifths supermajorities in both houses (36 Senate, 71 House needed).

S.note: Totals include the 25 holdovers (40-10 before). States Newsroom/Indiana Capital Chronicle reporting: Democrats gained 5, Republicans keep a 35-15 supermajority; election-night report said 'at least four'. Wikipedia's page lists 34 R + 15 D (one seat missing). Unofficial.

H.note: Was 70-30 at the last election (69 R, 30 D, 1 independent before this one). Democrats gained 16. Indiana Capital Chronicle and Wikipedia agree on 54-46. Unofficial.

in.note: House Republicans lose their two-thirds supermajority (first time since 2010): with 54 of 100 they can no longer make the two-thirds quorum (67) alone. Senate Republicans keep two-thirds (35 of 50; quorum 34).

S.note: Not up in 2026 (four-year terms, elected 2024; next election 2028). Current makeup per Wikipedia (Kansas Senate, as of Dec 2025).

H.note: Was 88-37. Democrats net +20 (unofficial; Secretary of State auditing three close House districts). Two-thirds is 84 to override a veto.

ks.note: House Republicans lose their veto-proof two-thirds supermajority (held 16 years). The Senate keeps one (31 of 40).

S.note: 19 of 38 up: R won 16, D 3; holdovers R 14, D 5. Was 32-6 before the election (Wikipedia; the multi-state page said 31-7). Spectrum News: Democrats flipped 2 Senate seats. Unofficial.

H.note: Was 80-20. Democrats flipped 7 seats and lost 1 open seat in eastern Kentucky (Spectrum News), net +6. Unofficial.

ky.note: Republicans keep two-thirds in both houses (a Kentucky veto override needs only a majority of members).

S.note: no 2026 election (next regular election 2027). Current makeup per Wikipedia: District 14 vacant since Sen. Larry Selders (D) died in July 2026; Wikipedia's infobox says 27 R, its roster 28.

H.note: no 2026 election (next regular election 2027). Current makeup per Wikipedia (Nov 12, 2026): vacancies HD 92 (Stagni, R, resigned June 2026), HD 77 (Wright, R, resigned Sept 2026), HD 103 (Bayham, R, died Nov 2026).

S.note: Wikipedia's 2026 page shows no change from 35-5, but may not be updated; no second source found (WBUR and the Boston Globe bar automated readers).

H.note: Wikipedia: D 137 (+3), R 21 (-4), 1 independent (unchanged), 159 of 160 accounted for; the missing seat is counted as uncalled. Was 134-25-1 at the last election. The Boston Globe described a 'punishing' night for House Republicans. Unofficial.

ma.note: Democrats keep veto-proof two-thirds in both houses.

S.note: All 47 seats up (four-year terms). Was 34-13; Democrat Lara Westdorp beat Sen. William Folden (R) in District 4. Wikipedia. The Maryland Manual's 2026 results page has no winners marked yet (its asterisks mark incumbents).

H.note: All 141 seats up. Was 102-39 (Wikipedia: D +4). Maryland Matters reported two Democratic pickups on election night (e.g. 33B) and more as mail ballots were counted. Unofficial.

md.note: Democrats keep their three-fifths veto-override majorities (29 Senate, 85 House).

S.note: Was 20 D, 14 R, 1 independent. Wikipedia's infobox says D 24 ('a supermajority, their first since 1985'), but its district table shows 23 D, 11 R and District 18 (held by independent Rick Bennett) uncalled. Two-thirds is 24 of 35.

H.note: No complete breakdown found. Democrats claimed at least 87 of 151 early Nov 4 (Bangor Daily News); a later States Newsroom report (AP calls) said at least 85; States Newsroom also reported House Republicans will hold 61 after losing about a dozen. Independents (3 before) inferred as the remainder. Excludes the non-voting tribal representatives. Unofficial.

me.note: Democrats expand both majorities. Senate two-thirds (24) depends on the uncalled District 18 race; House stays well short of two-thirds (101).

S.note: All 38 seats up. Was 20-18. Michigan Public: unofficial results show Democrats +3.

H.note: Was 58-52 Republican. Wikipedia and Ballotpedia (via search): 63-47. Michigan Public had 62 called for Democrats on Nov 5. Unofficial.

mi.note: House flips from Republican to Democratic control; Democrats win a trifecta (Speaker-elect Ranjeev Puri). No two-thirds majority.

S.note: D = DFL (Democratic-Farmer-Labor). All 67 seats up. Was 34-33. Unofficial; canvass Nov 19.

H.note: D = DFL. Was tied 67-67 (power-sharing). House Public Information (Nov 4): DFL 'on track' for 77-57; District 32A (Rep. Nolan West, R, ahead by 22 votes) is eligible for a recount. Unofficial; canvass Nov 19.

mn.note: House goes from a 67-67 tie (power-sharing) to a DFL majority; DFL trifecta. No two-thirds majority.

S.note: 17 of 34 up; totals include holdovers. Was 24-10. Democrats won the two seats needed to end the two-thirds majority (e.g. Keri Ingle beat Speaker Jon Patterson in SD 8).

H.note: Was 111-52. Democrats flipped 16 seats, their biggest House gain since 1974. Unofficial.

mo.note: Republicans lose their two-thirds veto-override supermajorities in both houses (Senate 23, House 109 needed); they keep control.

S.note: no 2026 election (next regular election 2027). Court-ordered special elections in November 2025 gave Democrats 2 seats (36-16 to 34-18), ending the Republican two-thirds. Now SD 34 is vacant after Juan Barnett (D) resigned (Wikipedia, Aug 2026).

H.note: no 2026 election (next regular election 2027). Nov 2025 court-ordered specials: a Democrat beat Rep. Jon Ray Lancaster (R, HD 22). Vacancies: HD 77 (R, died June 2026) and HD 70 (D, died June 2026). Nonpartisan special elections for both were held Nov 3, 2026; no results found.

ms.note: No 2026 change. The Senate Republican two-thirds ended in the November 2025 special elections; the House stays under Republican control.

S.note: 25 of 50 up; includes holdovers. Democrats flipped SD-10 and SD-29 (open seats). Was R 32-18.

H.note: MultiState: 55 R, 43 D, HD-20 (Keller, D, ahead by ~46) and HD-48 (Schomer, R, ahead by ~15) uncalled; Wikipedia's 56-44 assumes the leaders win. Democrats flipped HD-4. Was R 58-42.

mt.note: In 2025 nine Republican senators (censured by the state GOP) joined the 18 Democrats in a working majority. Of the nine, only Shelley Vance was up in 2026 and she lost her primary; the other eight hold over. With 20 Democrats, a similar bloc would still hold a majority, but no reporting yet says it will re-form. The Republican caucus re-elected Matt Regier Senate President on Nov. 11. Republicans are well short of the two-thirds of the whole Legislature (100 of 150) needed to refer constitutional amendments.

S.note: Uncalled: Sen. Danny Britt's (R, Robeson/Hoke/Scotland; reported as SD-24) seat, where he led Catina Hamm (D) by 228 votes on Nov. 11, inside the recount margin. If Britt holds, R 26-24 (most outlets and Wikipedia count it so); if Hamm wins, 25-25, and Democratic Lt. Gov. Rachel Hunt breaks ties. Was R 30-20, so the 3/5 veto-override supermajority (30) is gone either way.

H.note: Unofficial (WSOC, Wikipedia); Nelson Mullins estimated 70-49-1. About five races were within 1 point and could be recounted after the Nov. 13 canvass. Democrats take the majority (61) for the first time since 2010, one short of 3/5 (72). Was R 71-49.

nc.note: House flips to Democrats; Republican 3/5 veto-override supermajority lost in both chambers; Senate control hinges on the Britt race (a tie would give Democrats control via the Lt. Governor).

S.note: 24 of 47 up; includes holdovers. Democrat Mary Adams beat Sen. Jeff Barta (R) in SD-43. Was R 42-5.

H.note: MultiState: 80-12 with HD-41 (Fargo, two seats) still counting; Democrats Tiongson and Heidenreich led for both, Heidenreich by about 33 votes (possible recount). If both hold, 80-14. Democrats won HD-43's two seats, HD-25 (Mitskog over Skroch) and the HD-42 special; Republicans took one HD-11 seat. Before: 83 R, 10-11 D (one vacancy).

nd.note: Republicans keep two-thirds supermajorities in both chambers.

L.note: Officially nonpartisan; 24 seats up. By party registration, unofficial: 30 Republicans, 18 Democrats, 1 independent (Cindy Maxwell-Ostdiek, LD-4), down from 33 R / 15 D / 1 I. Republicans lost LD-4 (Sen. Brad von Gillern), LD-12 (Sen. Merv Riepe, to Christy Knorr) and LD-18 (to Jess Goldoni); LD-8 went from an independent to Democrat Erin Feichtinger. The Republican 33-vote filibuster-proof bloc is gone. An undated Nebraska Public Media report of 32 R / 17 D appears to be from an earlier cycle.

S.note: Democrats gained 7; no recounts requested. Was R 16-8. Short of 2/3 (16). Rebecca Perkins Kwoka (D) chosen President.

H.note: House Clerk Paul Smith's estimate (an earlier one was 291 D); 16 recounts requested as of Nov. 10, which could shift a few seats. Above 2/3 (267), a veto-proof majority for the first time. Was R 220-179 (before vacancies).

nh.note: Both chambers flip from Republican to Democratic; House Democrats gain a 2/3 supermajority.

S.note: no 2026 election; current makeup (222nd Legislature). Next election November 2027.

A.note: no 2026 election; current makeup after the November 2025 election (Democrats gained 5). Next election November 2027.

S.note: no 2026 election (four-year terms; next 2028), except a special election in SD-33 won by Rex Wilson (R), which didn't change the count. Current makeup.

H.note: Democrats flipped HD-7, HD-38, HD-39 and HD-57; Republicans flipped HD-4. Was D 44-26 (43-25 with two vacancies). 47 is exactly two-thirds.

nm.note: House Democrats reach a two-thirds supermajority (47 of 70).

S.note: 11 of 21 up; includes holdovers. Unchanged; one short of 2/3 (14).

A.note: Checked 2026-11-14 against opened sources (states/elected_2026_check.json): 31 D, 10 R, AD-22 uncalled (the Democrat leads by under 100 votes); Democrats have two-thirds either way. Nevada Independent (about Nov. 10): Democrats 32 of 42, counting AD-22, where Shenea Booth (D) led Assm. Melissa Hardy (R) by about 72 votes (MultiState still lists it uncalled: 31-10-1). Democrats flipped AD-2, AD-4, AD-13, AD-35 (and AD-22). Was D 27-15. Above 2/3 (28) either way.

nv.note: Assembly Democrats gain a two-thirds supermajority; Senate stays one short.

S.note: Uncalled: SD-43, where Devin Lander (D) narrowly led Sen. Jake Ashby (R) in later counts (Ashby led on election night); Wikipedia counts it D, 48-15. Democrats unseated six Republicans (SD-1, 9, 17, 38, 39, 44). Was D 41-22. Regains 2/3 (42).

A.note: Uncalled: AD-49 and AD-126, Democrats leading in both (Wikipedia and Greenberg Traurig count 111-39). Democrats gained seven seats (AD-3, 12, 16, 45, 46, 107, 143); Republicans gained AD-119. Was D 103-47. Above 2/3 (100).

ny.note: Senate Democrats regain a two-thirds supermajority; Assembly Democrats keep and widen theirs.

S.note: 16-17 of 33 up; includes holdovers. Democrats flipped SD-3 and SD-27 (Sen. Michele Reynolds lost). Was R 24-9. Republicans keep 3/5 (20).

H.note: MultiState: HD-29, HD-37, HD-44, HD-75 uncalled (Spectrum News on Nov. 4: 52 R, 42 D, five uncalled). Democrats flipped 8 seats. Was R 65-34. Republicans can reach at most 57, below 3/5 (60).

oh.note: House Republicans lose their 3/5 veto-override supermajority (with Democrat Amy Acton elected governor); Senate supermajority kept.

S.note: 24 of 48 up; includes holdovers. No seats changed.

H.note: Democrats gained six (five incumbents beaten: HD-75, 83, 84, 95, 100; open HD-64). Was R 81-20. Republicans keep 2/3 (68) but fall one short of the 3/4 (76) needed to pass revenue bills without a public vote.

ok.note: House Republicans lose the three-fourths majority for revenue bills; keep two-thirds.

S.note: 15 of 30 up; includes holdovers. Virginia Stapleton (D) beat Tracy Cramer (R), SD-11. Was D 18-12. Above 3/5 (18).

H.note: Democrats flipped HD-21 (Michael Welsh over Kevin Mannix) and HD-52 (Hank Sanders over Scott Hege). Was D 37-23 (36-24 at the 2024 election). Above 3/5 (36).

or.note: Democrats keep and widen their 3/5 revenue supermajorities in both chambers.

S.note: 25 of 50 up; Democrats won 16, Republicans 9; holdovers D 10, R 15. All races called by AP (Spotlight PA). No tie, so the Lieutenant Governor's tie vote isn't needed. First Democratic Senate majority since 1994.

H.note: AP as reported by Spotlight PA/Inquirer/WITF on Nov 4: at least 111-88 with a handful uncalled. Wikipedia's summary page gives 113-90 and its House election page a range of D 111-114, R 89-92. Control isn't in doubt.

pa.note: Senate flips R to D (26-24); Democratic trifecta with Gov. Shapiro

S.note: Republicans lost SD-17 and SD-34 (both deputy minority leaders).

H.note: Before 64-10-1. HD-42 R to D; HD-15 R to independent Allan Fung (a former Republican). HD-49 uncalled: Veronicka Vega (D) led independent Rep. Jon Brien by about 110 votes. Wikipedia's House page had no results yet; figures from MultiState.

S.note: Not up in 2026 (four-year terms; next election 2028). Current makeup.

H.note: Democrats flipped 10 seats (before 89-35), including Majority Leader Micah Caskey's. Reported as certified after recounts. 79 is below two-thirds (83 of 124).

sc.note: House Republicans lose their two-thirds supermajority

S.note: SD-11 uncalled: Chris Karr (R) led Aaron Matson (D) by a few dozen votes; SD-12 possible recount (R won by about 130). Republicans keep two-thirds either way.

H.note: Before 65-5. The uncalled seat (HD-11, second seat) is between two Republicans, so effectively 59-10-1 (Wikipedia's figure). The independent, Evangeline Poor Bear (HD-27), is described as aligned with Republicans. First Democratic legislative gains since 2008.

S.note: 17 of 33 up (with holdovers). No seats changed hands. Sen. Brent Taylor (R, SD-31) won a U.S. House seat; his Senate seat will be filled by special election, so it may be vacant at the start of 2027.

H.note: Six seats went R to D (before 75-24). Wikipedia's infobox lists 29 D and one write-in winner (a 'write-in gain'); the summary page gives 69-30. The write-in's identity and caucus weren't found. Republicans keep two-thirds (66 of 99); a veto override needs only a majority in Tennessee.

S.note: 16 of 31 up (with holdovers); before 20-11. The Texas Tribune (Nov 4): 'the line in the Texas Senate appeared to hold firm at 19 Republicans and 12 Democrats.'

H.note: Checked 2026-11-14 against opened sources (states/elected_2026_check.json): 79 D, 63 R, 8 uncalled (Wikipedia); Democrats hold the majority either way (76 needed). The Texas Tribune's 83-67 counted leads. A real Democratic majority, not a tie: first since 2003 (76 needed). 83-67 is the Texas Tribune's count if leads held (Nov 4: 11 AP-called flips, 3 concessions, at least 7 more uncalled Democratic leads); later reports say 83-84 D. Wikipedia's infobox read 79 D, 63 R with 8 seats not entered. Rep. Senfronia Thompson (D) is the presumptive Speaker, with 90 claimed pledges.

tx.note: House flips R to D (about 83-67); Senate stays R

S.note: 15 of 29 up (with holdovers); before 22 R, 6 D, 1 Forward. SD-5 (Millner's seat) and SD-19 (Majority Leader Cullimore) flipped R to D (MultiState). SD-11 uncalled: Brooks Benson (R) vs. Sen. Emily Buss (Forward). Republicans keep two-thirds (20 of 29) either way. Not certified until the canvass; derived from flips, no source states the total.

H.note: Checked 2026-11-14 against opened sources (states/elected_2026_check.json): 43 R, 26 D, 2 unaffiliated, 4 uncalled (HD-20, 48, 59, 61); Republicans lose two-thirds either way (at most 47 of 50 needed). Wikipedia (Nov 9): 44 R, 29 D, 2 independents (HD-3 and HD-38 went to unaffiliated candidates), but its results table gives ranges R 43-49, D 24-30, so a few seats (MultiState lists HD-20, 48, 59, 61) were still uncalled. Republicans lose two-thirds (50 of 75) even at the top of the range: 'For the first time since 1993, Republicans did not hold a supermajority in the Utah House.'

ut.note: House Republicans lose their two-thirds supermajority

S.note: no 2026 election (next 2027). Current makeup.

H.note: no 2026 election (next 2027). Current makeup; Wikipedia's member list showed District 20 vacant after Michelle Maldonado (D) resigned May 31, 2026, while its infobox gives 64-36 and names Sonia Vásquez Luna (D).

S.note: Preliminary. Democrats alone have two-thirds (20 of 30); with the Progressive, 21.

H.note: Seven Days (preliminary): 102 D, 7 Progressives, 3 independents, 38 R. Wikipedia gives 102-38-6-4. Close races: Hardwick (R led by 8 votes, likely recount) and southern Franklin County (D led by 2). D+P = 109, above two-thirds (100).

vt.note: Democrats (with Progressives) regain two-thirds supermajorities in both houses Democrats and Progressives together hold veto-proof majorities in both houses against Gov. Phil Scott (R), re-elected.

S.note: 24 of 49 up (with holdovers); Democrats flipped one seat (before 30-19). Two-thirds (33) wasn't within reach.

H.note: KUOW (Nov 9): Democrats 'on track to hold at least 66' of 98, a two-thirds majority, the first since 1949 (before 59-39).

wa.note: House Democrats gain a two-thirds supermajority

S.note: 17 of 33 up (with holdovers). Democrats flipped three seats (AP, preliminary). First Democratic Senate majority since 2008-10.

A.note: Democrats flipped eight seats and held all their own (before 54-45 R).

wi.note: Senate and Assembly flip R to D; Democratic trifecta with Gov.-elect David Crowley

S.note: About half up (with holdovers). Democrats doubled their caucus from 2 to 4; Republicans keep two-thirds.

H.note: Twelve seats flipped R to D (before 91-9 or 90-9-1 vacant). 21 Democrats means Republicans fall short of the four-fifths (80) needed to suspend the three-readings rule; they keep two-thirds. A veto override needs only a majority in West Virginia. Figures from Wikipedia; a States Newsroom report confirms 12 flips.

wv.note: House Republicans lose their four-fifths majority (rule suspension)

S.note: 16 of 31 up (with holdovers). No change.

H.note: Democrats picked up HD-11 by 54 votes (before 56-6). The August primary cut the Freedom Caucus's House bloc sharply (it lost about 13-14 incumbents; projected down from about 35 members to about 10), ending its House majority; it lost six Senate allies too. Traditional Republicans now lead both houses.

wy.note: Freedom Caucus loses control of the House (in the primary) Republican factions: Freedom Caucus vs. traditional Republicans; the Freedom Caucus lost its House majority in the August primary.
